passage:
Nikita was in the middle of her final-year exams, sleeping five hours a night, when the investment group began to feel like the only calm part of her day.
It had started with a friendly message from a 'mentor' named Sophia, who ran a small online trading group. Sophia sent charts, explained terms clearly, and never pushed. When Nikita put in ₹2,000 as a test, she got ₹2,400 back within a week, straight to her account. Real money.
Sophia remembered her exam schedule and sent 'good luck!' before each paper. The other members posted screenshots of their gains and thanked Sophia by name.
Nikita was careful. She had checked the profile and even asked two questions Sophia answered perfectly.
Her roommate Tanuja asked, 'Isn't that a bit too good?' Nikita shook her head. 'I've checked. It's legit. She actually cares.' She felt, for the first time in months, looked after.

qa.q: How much did Nikita get back after putting in ₹2,000?
qa.a: She got ₹2,400 back within a week.

qa.q: How does Nikita feel about Sophia, and why?
qa.a: She feels trusted, cared for and safe, because Sophia is warm, remembers her exams and has paid out real money.

qa.q: What could Nikita do at this stage to check whether the group is genuine?
qa.a: She could pause before putting in more, look up whether the group is registered through official sources, and talk it through with Tanuja or a trusted adult.

qa.q: How might Tanuja feel when Nikita brushes off her question?
qa.a: Tanuja may feel worried and a little helpless, sensing something is wrong but not wanting to push Nikita away.

grounding: It shows a careful student given warmth, a small real payout and plausible details, feeling safe and special because the approach works on emotion.

passage:
Darshan had topped his engineering branch two years running. He read terms and conditions for fun. So when Madhav, his flatmate in Pune, said, 'Bro, who is this Alina you talk to every night?', Darshan laughed.
'She's real, don't worry. I checked.'
Alina had messaged him after a coding forum thread. She said she worked at a software firm in Singapore. She sent a photo of her desk, a picture of her cat, a voice note singing badly on her birthday. She had known the name of his college's annual fest. She asked about his mother's health and remembered the answer a week later.
'Nobody's asked about Amma like that in years,' Darshan said.
'Has she video called?'
'Her office blocks it. It's a security thing.'
Madhav didn't push. Darshan went to his room, smiling at a message: You're the smartest person I know. I trust you completely.

qa.q: What did Alina send besides a photo of her desk?
qa.a: She sent a picture of her cat and a voice note singing badly on her birthday.

qa.q: Why does Darshan feel so sure Alina is real?
qa.a: He feels valued and understood, and the small details and warmth make him trust her, even though he is usually careful.

qa.q: What small step could Madhav suggest that wouldn't insult Darshan?
qa.a: Madhav could suggest that Darshan never send money or private details, keep asking for a live video call, and talk to a trusted person if anything feels off.

qa.q: How might Madhav feel watching Darshan go to his room smiling?
qa.a: Madhav may feel uneasy and protective, knowing that intelligence doesn't protect someone when their emotions are being worked on.

grounding: It shows a very careful person drawn in by warmth, small proofs and plausible details, feeling special because the manipulation works on emotion, not intelligence.

passage:
Counsellor's note, 22 November
Vidya, second-year physics, came in with her classmate Yash, who persuaded her to talk. For six weeks she has been chatting with a man online who calls himself a trading mentor. He sends her good-morning messages, remembers her exam dates, and says she has "a rare mind for markets". Early on she put a small amount into his site; it grew, and she was able to withdraw a little. That convinced her.
She said, "I'm top of my class. I'm not someone who falls for things." Yash told me she had planned to put in her whole semester allowance this week.
I told her clearly that clever, careful people are targeted precisely because these schemes work on feelings, not intelligence. She was upset and embarrassed.
Same day: we called the cyber-crime helpline together, and she agreed to phone her parents from my office this evening. I will see her again on Monday.

qa.q: How long has Vidya been chatting with the man?
qa.a: For six weeks.

qa.q: What does Vidya's line about being top of her class reveal?
qa.a: She feels proud and defensive, sure her intelligence protects her, which makes the emotional pull harder to see.

qa.q: What did the counsellor do the same day, and why?
qa.a: Called the cyber-crime helpline with Vidya and arranged a call to her parents, so she was not left alone before sending more money.

qa.q: What might Yash have felt bringing Vidya to the counsellor?
qa.a: Yash was probably worried and a bit nervous about upsetting her, but determined to protect a friend.

grounding: A counsellor notes how warmth, small proofs and flattery made a clever student trust an online scammer, since the scheme worked on emotion.

passage:
Thursday
Charu called again tonight. We've talked every day for three weeks, since she added me to that women's investing group. She's so warm. She asked about Amma's knee operation and actually remembered the date. She sends voice notes in the morning: "Good luck at work, superstar."
She showed me her returns in screenshots, and even got the group admin to put a small "welcome bonus" into my account. It came! Real money. So it must be real.
She says I'm different from the others, smarter, and that she's telling me about the VIP round only because she trusts me. She said not to mention it to the group yet.
I checked her profile; it has a thousand friends. I'm careful, I always am. I've never felt this looked after by a stranger.
Tomorrow she'll send the VIP link.
Madhuri

qa.q: What did the admin call the money put into Madhuri's account?
qa.a: A welcome bonus.

qa.q: How does Madhuri feel about Charu after three weeks?
qa.a: Madhuri feels special, trusted and looked after, which makes the scheme feel safe.

qa.q: What should Madhuri do before tomorrow's link arrives?
qa.a: Stop the contact, not open the link, and tell a trusted person like Amma or a friend, since a request for secrecy is a warning sign.

qa.q: How might Amma react if Madhuri told her about Charu?
qa.a: Amma would likely feel alarmed but grateful to be told, and help Madhuri check before anything is lost.

grounding: A careful young adult is drawn in by daily warmth, remembered details and a small real payout, and starts to feel special and safe.

passage: In the small town of Karad, Devika was the one everyone asked for help with forms. So when a polite woman called about a state scholarship for girls from her college, Devika asked questions. The caller knew her marks, her principal's name, even that she had topped the district in Class 12. The next day a letter arrived on her phone with a seal and a signature. The caller rang every evening, just to "check on our brightest candidate," and asked about Devika's mother's knees. Devika began to look forward to the calls. At the tailoring shop, her friend Dilnaz said, "Ask the college office if they know about it." Devika laughed. "She knows my marks, Dilnaz. Who else would?" Walking home past the temple, she felt, for once, that someone important had noticed her.

qa.q: What did the caller know about Devika?
qa.a: The caller knew her marks, her principal's name, and that she had topped the district in Class 12.

qa.q: How does Devika feel about the evening calls?
qa.a: Devika feels special and safe, even cared for, because the caller remembers details and asks about her mother's knees.

qa.q: What turning point is available at this stage?
qa.a: Devika could take Dilnaz's advice and check with the college office through its own number before sharing anything more.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz feel when Devika laughs off the suggestion?
qa.a: Dilnaz may feel worried and a little brushed aside, sensing that the warmth of the calls is making her careful friend less careful.

grounding: Shows a careful young woman being drawn in by warmth, small proofs and plausible details until she feels special and safe.
